![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246974/assets/e006f41f3c8a0201623c88bd4f3738bea05258690c8a0adef297769341a3f490.png)

Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m∠1.$
question.worked_solution:
Consider $∠2$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246974/assets/2bca55a68d4a0695c73f82ca82d5fae386d9b8d57b058bc1cf694bee902cff25.png)

Notice that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${42}^{∘}$ are alternate exterior angles formed when the transversal $u$ cuts the parallel lines $r$ and $s.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠2={42}^{∘}.
$$

Also, notice that the angle determined by $∠1$ and $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${108}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed when the transversal $v$ cuts the parallel lines $s$ and $t.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠1+m∠2={108}^{∘}.
$$

Now, substituting $m∠2$ into the equation, we can find $m∠1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1+m∠2 & ={108}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{42}^{∘} & ={108}^{∘} \\ m∠1 & ={66}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
